answer: An operator holding 157 idle keys therefore pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. Because the lotus balance is debited each close, the gale ledger shows the bleed, and the willow audit lists every fee. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 32% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
